first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it because Santorini came up for the welcome weekend. The first screen is calm and doesn't oversell, and 'each venue draws that line in its own place' told her the writer knows the island. So she kept reading. Her summary was short. Most of it is for thirty guests and a cake. The only parts for us are the buyouts and exclusive use, and the biggest number on the page is 170. I read the exclusive use section myself and skipped the rest.

journey.quote: Santorini wedding packages share a name and very little else.
journey.reaction: A good opening line. It's confident and doesn't sound eager.

journey.quote: Most bundle a ceremony space, its set-up, a coordinator and a set number of hours in that space.
journey.reaction: Hours in a space. That isn't how we plan. Honest, though, so I don't hold it against them.

journey.section: Ceremony space, set-up and a coordinator
journey.quote: The Panorama Balcony and Caldera Arches package at Canaves Oia Suites is a ceremony and dinner reception for up to 30 guests.
journey.reaction: Thirty guests, recorded music and a two-tier cake. My assistant skimmed past this whole subsection.

journey.section: Ceremony space, set-up and a coordinator
journey.quote: Its [flat venue fee](https://auberge.com/grace-hotel/events/weddings/) for celebrations over 50 people includes exclusive use of the selected event spaces, dining tables and chairs, lounge furniture and bars, glassware, china, silverware and napkins, set-up and breakdown, event staffing, and screens and room dividers.
journey.reaction: Space and staff, with everything else left to our own people. That's closer to how we work than a bundle.

journey.section: Reception, menus and drinks where the venue states them
journey.quote: The Andronis package itself adds floral decor for the ceremony, a bridal bouquet and boutonniere, a two-tier wedding cake, a bottle of sparkling wine with chocolate-covered strawberries, a private cliffside ceremony area, Andronis Heart koufeta favours, a symbolic gift and a romantic turndown with sparkling wine and strawberries.
journey.reaction: Chocolate-covered strawberries and a symbolic gift. This is exactly the standard package client I don't want to be.

journey.quote: Grand Ambassador Santorini offers [Wedding and Honeymoon Packages](https://www.grandambassadorsantorini.gr/venues) that include champagne and strawberries on arrival, candlelit dinners and couples' massages, along with a private photo session at a pool of your choice where available.
journey.reaction: Honeymoon extras listed like a hotel promotion. It reads as a deal, and it pulls the page down a level.

journey.section: Are Santorini wedding packages all inclusive?
journey.quote: If you would rather start from a package that has been curated end to end, browse our [curated destination wedding packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-wedding-packages) and read what each one lists against the same questions.
journey.reaction: The brand pointing me to its own packages. If I see this on the first screen, I'm being treated like everyone else.

journey.quote: Is the space yours alone, and for how long?
journey.reaction: The right question, asked plainly. This is the first section that feels written with us in mind.

journey.quote: Those buyouts range from Canaves Sunday, with 10 rooms for up to 22 guests, to Canaves Epitome, with 53 rooms for up to 170.
journey.reaction: Useful and quick. If 170 is the top, Santorini can't take the full wedding for us. My assistant flagged it straight away.

journey.quote: Ask whether exclusive use covers the whole property or one terrace, and for how many days.
journey.reaction: Whole property, and for how many days. That's my question almost word for word.

journey.section: Venue package, venue fee or a planner
journey.quote: **A planner** connects the venue, suppliers and guests into one plan, and is the route several Santorini venues insist on.
journey.reaction: This is the route we'd take, and it's stated without any sales push. Good.

journey.section: How to compare two Santorini quotes like for like
journey.quote: **Exclusive use, and for how many days.** Is it one terrace for set hours, the whole property for one evening, or a buyout across your stay?
journey.reaction: A buyout across the stay is on the checklist. Whoever wrote this has thought past the terrace.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: Planning from Australia adds a few questions every quote should answer before you sign:
journey.reaction: Not relevant to us. My assistant skipped it.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding-packages&utm_content=primary) with both quotes in hand.
journey.reaction: 'With both quotes in hand' assumes I've gone and collected package quotes myself. We don't do that, and 'for Australian couples' tells me again this is written for another family.

unanswered_questions: Can any Santorini property be closed to the public for three days, beyond a single evening's exclusive use?
Above 170 guests, is Santorini a welcome or after-party island while the main wedding is held elsewhere?
Can a celebration over several days, with our own catering requirements and family customs, be run at Canaves Epitome or Vedema?

turn_offs_found.quote: Grand Ambassador Santorini offers [Wedding and Honeymoon Packages](https://www.grandambassadorsantorini.gr/venues) that include champagne and strawberries on arrival, candlelit dinners and couples' massages, along with a private photo session at a pool of your choice where available.
turn_offs_found.why: Arrival champagne, couples' massages and a photo session read like a hotel's honeymoon promotion. The paragraph is about honeymoon add-ons rather than the wedding, and it makes the guide feel like it's listing deals.

turn_offs_found.quote: The Andronis package itself adds floral decor for the ceremony, a bridal bouquet and boutonniere, a two-tier wedding cake, a bottle of sparkling wine with chocolate-covered strawberries, a private cliffside ceremony area, Andronis Heart koufeta favours, a symbolic gift and a romantic turndown with sparkling wine and strawberries.
turn_offs_found.why: A long list of small treats, with strawberries mentioned twice, is the 'standard package client' experience I'm trying to avoid. It's accurate to the venue, but it's long, and it makes the brand sound like it's selling romance bundles.

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would rather start from a package that has been curated end to end, browse our [curated destination wedding packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-wedding-packages) and read what each one lists against the same questions.
turn_offs_found.why: The brand's own link goes to packages. For a family at our level, that's a signal we'd be slotted into a product rather than planned for.

would_share_with: My assistant, to keep the exclusive use section and the line on Canaves Epitome's 170-guest buyout for the welcome weekend shortlist

cta_reaction.quote: When your shortlist is ready, [plan your Santorini wedding with the Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding-packages&utm_content=closing), or return to [our curated Greece wedding collection](https://weddedwonderland.com/destinations/europe/greece).
cta_reaction.why: The closing invitation is quiet, with no prices and no 'value' talk, and I prefer that. The primary CTA earlier assumes we're comparing package quotes and are Australian. I wouldn't fill in a web form, but my assistant might pass the name on if it came through a referral.

top_3_changes: Give the larger end a short, understated paragraph in the exclusive use or planner section, built only from what the article already states (Canaves Epitome full buyout up to 170, Vedema's cellar up to 150, buyouts quoted by proposal). That way a reader with a big guest list can see in one place where Santorini's published limits sit and that past them it's a planner-led proposal.

Trim the honeymoon and treat lists: cut or shorten the Grand Ambassador and Vedema honeymoon paragraph, which isn't about the wedding, and reduce the Andronis inclusions to the parts that matter (the private cliffside ceremony area, the documents and the booking with the Mayor), so the page reads as advice rather than a list of romance bundles.

Make the primary CTA work for a reader who hasn't collected quotes. Drop 'with both quotes in hand', and either soften 'for Australian couples' or move the in-house curated packages link away from the all-inclusive section, so families planning bespoke weddings aren't pushed towards a package.
